messages.author: bc810b1d0900407f
messages.subject: SRMR in lavaan
parts:
Hi All,

I would like to ask a quick question regarding SRMR in lavaan. I know lavaan can compute several different versions of SRMR. I would like to focus on single-group path models with some exogenous variables treated as fixed. This is an illustration:

``` r
library(lavaan)
#> This is lavaan 0.6-19
#> lavaan is FREE software! Please report any bugs.
model <-
"
x4 ~ x1 + x2 + x3
x5 ~ x4
x6 ~ x5
"
fit <- cfa(model,
           data = HolzingerSwineford1939,
           meanstructure = TRUE)
out <- fitMeasures(fit,
                   c("srmr",
                     "srmr_bentler",
                     "srmr_bentler_nomean",
                     "srmr_mplus",
                     "srmr_mplus_nomean"))
print(cbind(out))
#>                            out
#> srmr                0.05609851
#> srmr_bentler        0.05609851
#> srmr_bentler_nomean 0.06360973
#> srmr_mplus          0.05609851
#> srmr_mplus_nomean   0.06360973

fit_nomean <- cfa(model,
                  data = HolzingerSwineford1939,
                  meanstructure = FALSE)
out2 <- fitMeasures(fit_nomean,
                    c("srmr",
                      "srmr_bentler",
                      "srmr_bentler_nomean",
                      "srmr_mplus",
                      "srmr_mplus_nomean"))
print(cbind(out2))
#>                           out2
#> srmr                0.06360973
#> srmr_bentler        0.06360973
#> srmr_bentler_nomean 0.06360973
#> srmr_mplus          0.06360973
#> srmr_mplus_nomean   0.06360973
```

Is the element "srmr" in fitMeasures() output simply a placeholder that does not correspond to any specific version of SRMR, but stores one of the versions of SRMR internally computed, depending on the model and other settings?

-- Shu Fai

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: RE: SRMR in lavaan
parts:
> Is the element "srmr" in fitMeasures() output simply a placeholder that does
> not correspond to any specific version of SRMR, but stores one of the versions
> of SRMR internally computed, depending on the model and other settings?

The 'default' SRMR is always one of the others, but which one, depends on the context. The relevant part of the code in lav_fit_srmr.R is this:

# srmr
if (lavobject@Options$mimic %in% c("lavaan", "EQS")) {
if (categorical) {
indices["srmr"] <- SRMR_BENTLER_NOMEAN
} else {
indices["srmr"] <- SRMR_BENTLER
}
} else if (lavobject@Options$mimic == "Mplus") {
if (lavobject@Options$information[1] == "expected") {
if (categorical) {
indices["srmr"] <- SRMR_BENTLER_NOMEAN
} else {
indices["srmr"] <- SRMR_BENTLER
}
} else {
if (categorical) {
indices["srmr"] <- SRMR_MPLUS_NOMEAN
} else {
indices["srmr"] <- SRMR_MPLUS
}
}
} # Mplus only

So by default, SRMR = SRMR_BENTLER. But this changes to SRMR_BENTLER_NOMEAN in the categorical setting. If you use mimic="Mplus", other choices are made.

Yves.
